title: Where state lives, and swapping out whole
summary: An MU is a processing unit that hosts MIs and is disposable, like an MI (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25), so it holds nothing that cannot be rebuilt or moved: a Demand stateWhere is FABRIC, CHECKPOINT or TEMPORARY; LOCAL is refused. A task whose state survives is deactivated whole (Aglets swap-out): its hook runs, its state is written and verified against a digest, its RAM is released; ACTIVATE_TASK resumes it here or anywhere. The arbitrator prefers swapping out a lower-importance task to adding swap and to making a more important demand wait, and asks the cluster where the swapped-out task resumes. TEMPORARY tasks keep dev1 behaviour: swap is added, or the cluster is asked to move them and the new start is WAITING.
authority: built and tested offline (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-25)
invariants: State is verified against a digest before RAM is released, and before a task resumes
Each swap-out asks the cluster where the task resumes
procedure: Give every demand its real stateWhere; it decides whether it can be swapped out or moved
